clue.text: With compulsion, former pupil scattered seeds around front of school

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: the shuffled seeds are placed on either side of the school's initial
seeds that are scattered are strewn about, so these letters are rearranged
the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An ex-pupil compulsively scatters seeds around the school entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With compulsion' reads as the start of the wordplay but is the definition; OB, an old boy, is the usual crossword former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obsessed acts under a fixation or irresistible urge, which is what compulsion describes.

clue.text: New horse curb required ---- bits catalogued herein

indicators.note: a new version of the words is made by reworking their letters

explanation.surface: A rider needs a fresh curb bit and looks it up in a catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: A curb is a type of bit for a horse, so the surface is about tack; the dashes stand for a break in the printed clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A brochure is a promotional booklet listing goods, so items such as bits would be catalogued in one.

clue.text: A number engaged in a row

definitions.meaning: a cardinal number, one more than seven
a rowing crew of oarsmen pulling together in one boat

explanation.definitionFit: Eight is both the numeral after seven and the name for a rowing boat's crew.

clue.text: Another view of what's in store

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a further look and the psychic gift of seeing the future.

clue.text: Exhibition play about a girl loved by Zeus

indicators.note: the play wraps round the girl, as about means surrounding

parts.note: a play is a drama
Io was a maiden Zeus loved in Greek myth, turned into a heifer

explanation.surface: A theatre exhibits a play about one of Zeus's mythological lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional scene displayed for viewing, a kind of museum exhibit.

clue.text: Victorian fashion causing a stir

definitions.meaning: a padded frame worn under the back of a nineteenth-century skirt

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a padded Victorian skirt support and energetic fuss.

clue.text: Invite offer

definitions.meaning: to ask someone along, an old sense
a price proposed at an auction

explanation.definitionFit: Archaically one may bid guests to come, and a bid is an offer at auction.

clue.text: An oriental plant canna is to replace

indicators.note: to replace these letters is to put them in a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener plans to swap out an Eastern canna lily.
explanation.definitionFit: Santonica is a wormwood of Asia whose flower heads yield a medicinal drug.

clue.text: Police club in India

parts.note: looks like a social club for officers, but means the heavy stick Indian police carry

explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is a long bamboo staff bound with iron, used as a weapon by police in India.

clue.text: Society of criminals — could make one's hair curl

definitions.meaning: a Chinese secret society linked with organised crime
a curling iron or pair of ... for the hair

explanation.definitionFit: A tong is a Chinese criminal brotherhood, and also a single form of hair tongs used for curling.

clue.text: Decoration handed out to correspondent

indicators.note: things handed out are distributed, so the word's letters are dispersed into a new order

explanation.surface: A medal is presented to a newspaper's foreign reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondent' suggests a journalist, but it is used as an adjective meaning matching.
explanation.definitionFit: Coordinate as an adjective means equal in rank or corresponding, matching correspondent in that sense.

clue.text: Keep discussion going on setting for the stone

definitions.meaning: to continue talking, read as two words
the bezel of a ring that holds a gem

explanation.definitionFit: Read as a phrase it means keep talking; as one word it is a jeweller's term for a gem's mount.

clue.text: Roast lamb is a dish fit for the gods when cooked without salt

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared and changed into something new

parts.note: these letters are the ones left out of the mix, signalled by without

explanation.surface: A roast lamb dish is heavenly even when made unsalted.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of ROAST LAMB IS A, once 'without' removes the letters of SALT, rearrange ('cooked') to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ambrosia was the food of the Olympians, granting immortality.

clue.text: Tall boy can train to be expert in this way at Kew?

definitions.text: expert in this way at Kew?

indicators.note: to train is to bring into shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the words as the setter meant them, with the I that the printed clue lacks

explanation.surface: A tall lad can be trained up to be a Kew gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the fodder lacks an I, so the clue has lost a word (probably 'I'); 'train' rearranges the letters. Kew Gardens in London is a famous botanical garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Kew's experts study plants, so their way of knowing is in terms of plant science.

clue.text: Broken shank in a vessel is needed for a car

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the vessel

parts.note: a craft is a boat or vessel

indicators.note: a broken shank is in pieces, so its letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A ship's broken shank needs a part sourced from a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges the shank's letters and 'in' sets them inside the vessel's word; the definition is loose, naming the answer as a part a car needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A car engine's main rotating shaft turns the pistons' movement into rotation, so it is a part every car needs.

clue.text: She's a minder working with us

indicators.note: letters working are put to use in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman describes herself as a childminder employed alongside us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges A MINDER plus US; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after children is a nursemaid, so the pronoun she stands for her.

clue.text: Politicians imposed on one — the devils!

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Politicians impose upon a single person, those devils!
explanation.walkthrough: 'imposed on' puts MPS after I in a down-the-page sense; here, in an across, it simply follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Imps are little demons or mischievous devils.

clue.text: Parking on hill top, brought back windflowers — wondrous things

parts.note: P is the map abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
brought back means the word for windflowers is read in reverse

parts.note: the anemone is called the windflower

explanation.surface: Someone parks on a hilltop and gathers windflowers, marvelling at the view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns ANEMONE into ENOMENA; the plural in the clue is loose for one flower's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable occurrences or marvels.

clue.text: Employer helping to form the house rules

indicators.note: the words help make up the answer, as its letters sit inside them

explanation.surface: An employer has a hand in drawing up the office rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'house rules': hoUSE Rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is one who employs or makes use of something.

clue.text: Force battles on again, given fruit

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravitational force
re-engages means joins battle once more

explanation.surface: A force returns to the fight, awarded fruit as a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Greengages are green plums, a type of fruit.

clue.text: Philosopher who took ages to sum up

parts.note: eras are long ages

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written upwards, reversing it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A philosopher took a long time to summarise his thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SUM to MUS beneath ERAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was a Renaissance humanist scholar and thinker.

clue.text: Food at the golf club — or this brew-up?

definitions.text: Food at the golf club — or this brew-up?

parts.words: Food at the golf club — or this brew-up?
parts.note: teatime refreshment served out on the course, punning on the putting surface and the drink

explanation.definitionFit: Tea served at a golf club could be called tea on the green, while the term itself is an unfermented Chinese brew.

clue.text: Hands up! It's an advantage for a boxer

definitions.meaning: the command to stretch out the arms
the length of a fighter's arm span

explanation.definitionFit: Reach means stretching the arms out and also a boxer's arm length, a real edge in the ring.

clue.text: Oil the wheel

definitions.meaning: a laxative oil from a bean
a small swivelling wheel under furniture

explanation.definitionFit: Castor names both a medicinal oil and a swivel wheel fitted to chair legs.

clue.text: Has turned up in the same place: Here's the man's address

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read upwards, reversing the word

parts.note: ib, short for ibidem, means in the same place in references

explanation.surface: A man turns up at the same spot, giving his address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses HAS to SAH; 'Here's' only joins. 'address' means a form of address, not a location.
explanation.definitionFit: In colonial India sahib was a respectful title used when speaking to a man.

clue.text: Sky-diver as usual on a higher plane?

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper who jumps from aircraft
normal means typical or as usual

explanation.surface: A parachutist goes about business as usual, high above in a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft, but the definition means a level beyond normal experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Paranormal events lie beyond scientific explanation, as if on another level of reality.

clue.text: Peculiar ring the theologian put on

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is placed on the first

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
DD stands for Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A divine wears an unusual ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd and peculiar are synonyms, both meaning strange.

clue.text: Sounds as if the man had notice

indicators.note: says the words that follow are to be judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: he'd is the contraction of he had

explanation.surface: Apparently that fellow had received a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay heed is to take notice or attention.

clue.text: Sheltered, in these times, in outhouse

indicators.note: the era abbreviation goes inside the outbuilding

parts.note: a shed is a small outbuilding
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: Someone takes shelter in a garden outhouse these days.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaded means screened from sun, thus protected or sheltered.

clue.text: Say nothing about prohibition covering English seed

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and mixed

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: the ban encloses the English abbreviation

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about a ban affecting English seed imports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here is an anagram signal, not a container: the O is mixed in with the letters of 'Say', while 'covering' puts E inside the ban.
explanation.definitionFit: The soya bean is the edible seed of a leguminous Asian plant.
